title: Data Models and Storage Engines

weeks.focus: Model and freeze workloads, access paths, and physical predictions
Build persistent B+ tree and LSM mechanisms
evidence: Internals review and Week 26 learning log
Evaluation, remediation, and Week 28 learning log

readiness_note: Ready on 2026-08-02 after semantic review, 11 storage-lab tests across 22 strict scenarios, six isolated evaluator invocations with stable calibration bands, two calibration checks, focused validation, full-course validation, resource verification, and evidence-safety review.

outcomes.statement: Derive logical and physical data models from quantified access paths, invariants, retention, growth, and ownership.
Explain and measure how pages, records, buffer pools, locality, and cache policy shape physical work.
Implement and validate a persistent paged B+ tree with point lookup, range scan, splits, cache behavior, deletion, and clean reopen.
Implement and validate an LSM store with memtable, SSTables, sparse indexes, Bloom filters, tombstones, and compaction.
Calculate read, write, and space amplification and connect them to tail latency, capacity, cost, and SSD endurance.
Choose indexes and diagnose query plans whose estimates, statistics, or access paths do not match the workload.
Diagnose read, write, range, skew, delete, cache, Bloom, compaction, and tombstone behavior from preserved same-input evidence.
Defend a storage-engine decision covering security, operations, cost, ownership, migration, rollback, recovery requirements, and reversal evidence.

resources.title: Database File Format
resources.purpose: Ground pages, B-tree cells, and record boundaries in a stable implementation contract.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 1.2, 1.6, and 2.1; sketch a page and name two choices the format does not prescribe for this lab.

resources.title: B+Tree Indexes
resources.purpose: Observe insertion, split, deletion, and composite-index reasoning from a database-internals course.
resources.assignment: Watch through deletion and composite indexes; predict changed pages for one insert/delete and compare with the lab trace.

resources.title: Database Systems Spring 2026 Schedule and Materials
resources.purpose: Connect storage, memory management, and indexes in one primary teaching sequence.
resources.assignment: Use only Database Storage I-II, Memory Management, and Indexes & Filters I-II notes/slides; produce a physical-path diagram and workload-dependent question.

resources.title: The Log-Structured Merge-Tree
resources.author_or_publisher: P. O'Neil, E. Cheng, D. Gawlick, E. O'Neil
resources.purpose: Derive the buffered write mechanism and original cost assumptions.
resources.assignment: Read the Abstract and Sections 1-3; derive why buffering changes write cost and list assumptions that differ from the lab.

resources.title: RocksDB Overview
resources.purpose: Compare operated LSM compaction shapes and amplification trade-offs.
resources.assignment: Read Architecture and Compaction Styles; compare leveled, tiered/universal, and FIFO under three amplification dimensions.

resources.title: Compaction
resources.purpose: Expose bytes, run shapes, and temporary space involved in compaction.
resources.assignment: Read Overview through Tiered+Leveled; draw one merge and identify temporary-space exposure.

resources.title: Write Stalls
resources.purpose: Relate compaction debt to bounded admission and operator-owned recovery.
resources.assignment: Read the complete page; map every trigger to a metric, owner, and safe overload action.

resources.title: Indexes
resources.purpose: Connect index operator/order support to update and storage costs.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 11.1-11.5; design equality and ordered-range indexes and explain their write/storage cost.

resources.title: Using EXPLAIN
resources.purpose: Ground query-plan diagnosis in estimated and actual physical work.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 14.1.1-14.1.3; compare estimated/actual rows and record one alternative explanation before changing an index.

resources.title: Statistics Used by the Planner
resources.purpose: Explain selectivity, correlation, and extended-statistics trade-offs.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 14.2.1-14.2.2; explain one correlation error and the cost of more detailed statistics.

resources.title: Overcoming the Write Amplification Problem with NVM Express Flexible Data Placement
resources.author_or_publisher: Amber Huffman and Chris Sabol; NVM Express
resources.purpose: Separate host/engine amplification from device media amplification.
resources.assignment: Read through the WAF definition and FDP mechanism; state which level the lab can measure and which remains unknown.

failure_experiments.evidence: same-input cache pair, page reads, hit/miss/eviction, warm and post-scan behavior, correctness, and recovery
same-input compaction pair, runs, pending bytes, stalls, amplification, temporary space, foreground tail, and recovery
same-input Bloom pair, filter checks/negatives/false positives, table probes, latency, and zero false negatives
same-input compaction pair, merge sources, table probes, ordered results, bytes, and range tail
same-input skew/cache pair, distribution, page hits/misses, splits/writes, post-scan state, and alternatives
same-input delete/compaction pair, tombstones, live/disk bytes, point/range/reopen absence, zero resurrection, and safe reclamation
